message.content: I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K and bought 44 shares of AAPL, which filled at my $223.00 limit for about $9,812 — within the mandate's $10,000 per-order cap, buy-only, at a price essentially at the market (last $222.70, ask $222.72), funded from existing cash with no money leaving the account, and the only trade today so total daily exposure is far below $20,000. The decision rested on FY2024 net sales of $391,035 million (+2% YoY), operating income of $123,216 million (up from $114,301 million), gross margin expanding to 46.2% on Services strength (Services +13% to $96,169 million at 73.9% margin), operating cash flow of $118,254 million, and diluted EPS of $6.08 / net income of $93,736 million — the slight EPS decline being attributable to a one-time $10.2B State Aid tax charge rather than operating deterioration, alongside $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities and a $110B buyback authorization with a raised $0.25 quarterly dividend; the main risks I noted are the DOJ/EU DMA antitrust matters and an 8% decline in Greater China sales.
